Subject: Initial load profile and some contract questions

Karthik — great conversation today, thanks for walking through Redwood's warm-pool model. Per our call, attaching the Q4 load profile from production so you can validate burst sizing. Two quick questions up-front: 1) do you have a hard SLA we can reference for scaled concurrency (we need 95th p90 token latency under 350ms for our checkout flow), and 2) can warm pools be pre-warmed in our VPC private deployment (we need on-prem-like controls)?

Thanks,
Emma

Acme Retail

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Initial load profile and some contract questions

Emma — thanks for the profile, I pulled it into our test harness and had Marissa run a quick throughput pass. High-level answers while we schedule a deeper run:

- SLA / SLO: we can commit to a latency SLO tailored to the checkout route. Based on the initial numbers, targeting p95 token latency < 350ms is achievable on our Dedicated nodes with a warm pool configuration; we typically codify this as an SLO in the contract (example: p95 < 350ms for 95% of rolling 1h windows). Marissa, can you confirm the baseline test we ran?

- Warm pools in Private: yes — for Private (VPC) deployments we support customer-controlled warm pools. Those are customer-managed instances that Redwood can orchestrate; they remain in the deployment and are kept primed. For strict air-gapped on-prem, we have a similar flow but need a short ops checklist.

Quick follow-ups / next steps:
1) Marissa to run a defined p95 stress pass against the attached profile and share latency/queueing curves (action: Marissa, ETA 48 hours).
2) Engineering doc with proposed contract SLO language and warm-pool operational notes (action: Kar thik, ETA EOD Thu).
3) Procurement Qs for contract: any required uptime credits / ramp windows (action: Ben to shadow and provide sample SLA clause).

I also attached a short one-pager on Redwood's burst-priming approach. Will loop back with the test artifacts.

Attachments: redwood-burst-priming-one-pager.pdf (PDF, 42KB)

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Emma Cole <emma@acme-retail.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Initial load profile and some contract questions

Emma — I ran the initial pass against the Q4 profile you sent. Short findings: we replayed 2 weeks of traffic scaled to your reported peak concurrency and focused on the checkout prompt (streaming off). Results:

- Baseline Dedicated nodes (no warm pool): p95 token latency ~ 460ms during spikes; queue depth increased and we saw transient 5–10s tail events while we spin up new workers.
- With warm pool (prewarmed small instances equal to 20% of steady-state concurrency): p95 token latency drops to ~320ms, tail events eliminated in our run, and measured scale-up time to full capacity reduced from ~28s to ~6–8s.
- Streaming considerations: when responses stream, we see increased first-byte variance; recommended approach is prefix-caching for checkout prompts to shave ~40–60ms off first byte.

See attached CSV charts and a short notes section in the Drive link. Observations / risks: warm pools materially reduce scale-up time and queueing but increase steady cost; we can propose an escape hatch where warm pools only activate for high-value routes.

Suggested acceptance criteria (can be contractized):
- p95 token latency < 350ms measured across rolling 1h windows for checkout route when warm-pool configured.
- Scale-up time to 90% capacity < 10s from spike detection (measured in production).
- Queueing latency contribution < 50ms when warm pool active.

Next steps (concrete):
1) I'll package the test artifacts and measured curves into the Drive folder (action: Marissa, ETA Tue EOD).
2) Kar thik to draft SLO clause language for inclusion in the MSA (action: Karthik, ETA Thu).
3) Ben to draft a sample pricing addendum that shows cost delta with/without warm pool (action: Ben, ETA Fri).

EMMA — can you confirm which routes we want considered "high-value" for warm-pool gating and whether procurement needs an initial cost estimate before legal review?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Cole <emma@acme-retail.com>

Thanks team — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of answers and clarifications:

- High-value routes: checkout confirmation, fraud-check microflow, and cart-resume should be gated by the warm-pool policy. Those three routes represent ~72% of the latency-sensitive revenue paths.
- Procurement: Liam would like an estimated monthly delta for warm-pool ops (ballpark is fine) ahead of the legal SLA draft. Liam, can you confirm if a 30-day baseline estimate is adequate?

We'd like Redwood to produce the SLO clause and the pricing addendum as separate artifacts so legal can review in parallel. Also, can you include a short runbook paragraph describing how to flip the warm-pool gating on/off for specific routes?

Emma
